candidate_windows.window_text: TAF introduces additional computation overhead to conventional SMT. We report the average wall-clock time of generating a full hypothesis with RALCP+TAF versus the base RALCP policy on different combinations of MT models and a 7B LLM. We run experiments on an A6000 GPU and an AMD EPYC 9354 32-Core CPU. The results are shown in Table 1. When using a small MT model Transformer-Big (0.2B), 7B LLM introduces significant computational overhead. As the size of the MT model gets larger, the relative overhead reduces.

We trained our NMT models (Transformer, $12 \times 6$ layers, $d_{\mathrm{model}} = 1024$ , $d_{\mathrm{inner}} = 4096$ , $n_{\mathrm{heads}} = 16$ ) with Adam optimizer and inverse square root annealing (Vaswani et al., 2017) with $7.5\mathrm{K}$ warmup steps and a maximum learning rate of $10^{-3}$ . The models were trained for a maximum of $100\mathrm{K}$ steps with a dropout of 0.1 on intermediate activations and label smoothing with $\alpha = 0.2$ . Our $\mathrm{De} \rightarrow \mathrm{En}$ models used joint BPE vocabulary of 16384 tokens and $\mathrm{En} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Zh} / \mathrm{Ja}$ used separate vocabularies with the same number of tokens per language.
